Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary For tips on how to play madeira, see Tips_madeira Contents 1 Elements of Game play 1.1 Pirates 1.2 City Watch 1.3 Windmill 1.3.1 During phases B, C or D 1.3.2 During phases B or C only 2 Game play 2.1 Phase A: Setup and Guild Choice 2.2 Phase B: Character Actions 2.2.1 Passing 2.3 Phase C: Building Actions 2.4 Phase D: Maintenance 2.5 Phase E: Crown's Requests 3 Game End 4 Reference Sheet 4.1 Crown’s Requests 4.2 Guild Favours 4.3 Passing 4.4 King’s Rewards Elements of Game play Pirates Pirates are black marks that indicate your failure to pay debts e.g., to feed your workers or pay the cost of an action. They have no effect on your score until game end. Pirate dice are black dice placed in the City Watch , which may be used by any player to take actions in Phase B . They will only give pirates to players if they fail to pay a building cost in Phase C . City Watch Whenever you place a worker in the City Watch, you may discard 3 pirates. Workers placed here have two uses: Phase B : send a worker from the City Watch home to make use of a pirate die. Phase D : send a worker from the City Watch home to gain 4 PP. Windmill Your standing on the Windmill indicates how many workers on the board you can feed automatically in Phase D , without needing additional bread. In addition, you may use the windmill to take one or more free actions during a turn: During phases B, C or D Exchange 2 goods for 1 good of a different type. Goods: wheat, sugar, wine Move up 1 step on the Windmill by discarding 2 wheat. If you are already on the top step, gain 1 PP instead. During phases B or C only Move down 1 step to gain 1 bread or 3 reals. If you are already on the bottom step, lose 1 PP to take this action. Gaining only 1 bread or 1 real. Game play Phase A: Setup and Guild Choice The four character tiles are randomly distributed among the five buildings One remains empty each turn, as indicated by the roman numeral on its top right. 3 pirate dice are rolled and placed in the City Watch. 3 guild dice per player are rolled and placed in rows on the Guild Board. Each player in turn places their marker on a row and selects the corresponding dice and one request. If the guild symbol matches any of their guild favours they flip them face up. Phase B: Character Actions Following the new turn order established in Phase A , players either select a character action or pass. A character action is selected by placing on it either a guild die (at the cost of a worker in the City Watch) or a pirate die. If a guild die is used, the player also places an action marker on the building space (to be resolved in Phase C ). You may activate a character with a die whose value is equal to or greater than the number of that character’s region (1, 2 or 3). You may also use a lower-numbered die by paying the difference in bread. A character may have a maximum of 1 pirate die on it, and a maximum number of dice equal to the number of players. A player may choose one of two possible character actions: Trigger the action specific to the character. Harvest: all fields in that region will yield one unit per worker, either: Wood (if they have not yet been cleared) or Crop (wheat, sugar or wine). One building each round contains no character card, so it only offers the harvest action, plus a bonus: one field is harvested twice. Steward a space to plant. Mayor city spot. Commander ship spot. Guild master wood. Passing To pass, a player chooses a free spot in the passing column: they may either choose to gain reals, or take the action depicted. The new turn order will be observed for the rest of the round and the beginning of the next. [Rating: 1/10] That dice rolling mechanic - UGH.  I hate, hate, hate, HATE this game.  It's very rare that I steadfastly refuse to play a game again after 1 playthrough when everybody else in my group is asking to try it out, but this is one of them.  Don't even get me started on the fact that they don't give you enough tokens, or that it's at its core just another spreadsheet type of game.    This is one of those games that, on its surface, seems to be dressed up with all sorts of great things, but when you get past the fancy coverings, realize that there is nothing of any real value there.

[Rating: 1/10] Extremely annoying game. It's hard to do the actions you want in a round without taking pirate tokens which then require actions to get rid of. Your cost for actions is determined by rolling dice AFTER you've taken the action - ridiculous! Lots of piddly rules. Too many steps to go through a round. Iconography isn't much help. Madeira will drive you to drink!

[Rating: 2/10] Second time ever playing though I didn't remember the first.  Let me first say that likely my impression was coloured by the circumstances of the play. K wanted to play it to see if he should buy it. He was insistent though it was after 11 that night. It would have been better if it was one of the first games of the night. We broke one of our rules to not learn a new game after dinner never mind close to midnight.  Of course K worked through the rules so he trounces J and me. It wasn't even close. [Rating: 2/10] This is just a box of mechanics wrapped up in a thin veneer of theme and, in my opinion, none of them are the slightest interesting or intuitive.   Played it twice now and the second time was even worse. I was so incredible bored that I actually developed a migrain. At least it comfirmed that this is one game I will never play again. Not even on a dare.

[Rating: 2/10] Like getting kicked in the teeth for two and a half hours.  If you play your first round wrong you will be continuously punished for the rest of the excruciatingly long playtime.

[Rating: 2.3/10] 4h30 à 3 sans les explications. Rien qui ne me fasse peur.  Du random, du hasard, de l'arbitraire, des petits poitns derègles petes couilles de partout (et donc des oublis).  J'ai aussi un doute sur les équilibrage (Fortalenza / PV Via citée controlées semble plus fort) mais j'ai pas assez derecul pour être catégorique.  J'aurrais bien aimé pas finir la partie ...  Un storyteling / matos de qualité.  Bref il devrait s'appeler Terraforming Madeira ce jeu ...

[Rating: 3/10] Another overwrought euro with nothing but the complexity standing out. Really there is nothing here I have not seen before. Why bother.

[Rating: 3/10] Madeira is complex and long, difficult to teach and learn, difficult to intuitively grasp without multiple plays, and harsh to those who don't calculate their resource conversions exactly. To make a decision about where to put a worker or when to pass, you need to consider the dozen different systems your decision will affect. A dozen is too many.  At the end of one game, one person had 1 pirate point, while everyone else had 0, so that person lost 16 victory points. This does not encourage making moves by intuition. [Rating: 3/10] Way too fiddly; worker placement meets vp salad. Theme felt pasted on, with no relation to history. Ack.

[Rating: 3/10] Yawn. Don't play this game if you have epilepsy because you'll have a seizure looking at the board. Just way too busy and too many different things to decipher. Definitely not my kind of game.

[Rating: 3/10] Mechanics don't mesh, none felt interesting. Doesn't feel quite unbalanced. Randomness doesn't fit with heavy game. Most rules seem overly complicated. We stopped after round 3 because we did not enjoy playing this game. I won't ever play again.
